rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Source-verification maintainer block on any student-facing file with practitioner citations.
rules_evaluated.evidence: HARM the rule prevents: a source drifts or reverses in the real world and the curriculum keeps citing it unchallenged because the freshness ledger never flags it for re-check (the compendium's own worked example: an Amp stance reversed and "the lecture taught the camp in present tense for three months" because its due-date arithmetic was built not to ask). That harm is PRESENT here, not hypothetical: two of the three `due:` stamps are computed as `checked`+6mo instead of `publication`+6mo, which §11a explicitly names as the one arithmetic to never use ("the arithmetic grants a three-weeks-from-stale source a fresh year, most confidently on the sources someone bothered to re-check"). klaassen-how-every-codes: published 2025-12-11 (verified live via WebFetch page metadata, `published_at: 2025-12-11T11:00:00.000-05:00`) → correct due = publication+6mo = 2026-06-11, which as of today (2026-08-28) is already ~2.5 months PAST due — yet the stamp reads `due:2027-01-30` (= checked:2026-07-30 + 6mo exactly), hiding that overdue status for another five months. geoffintech-charles: published 2026-04-09 (as stated in the citation) → correct due = 2026-10-09, but the stamp reads `due:2026-11-25` (= checked:2026-05-25 + 6mo exactly), granting ~6 weeks of unearned runway. Control check: curran-2x's own math is CORRECT (published 2026-04-16, verified live; due:2026-10-16 = publication+6mo exactly, NOT checked+6mo which would read 2026-11-25) — confirming this is a real per-citation arithmetic defect, not a misreading on this judge's part.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recompute `due:` from PUBLICATION date, not `checked` date, for the klaassen and geoffintech-charles stamps (klaassen → due:2026-06-11, already elapsed, route to immediate re-verification per §11a rather than a forward date; geoffintech-charles → due:2026-10-09). Leave curran-2x's stamp as-is; it is already correct.
